meta.method: Daily 7-day flood-risk forecast. No weather model is run here: published forecasts are combined with FloodTrace's own satellite-rain history. The ECMWF IFS 0.25 deg ensemble (control + 50 members) is fetched once for all 68 IMERG 0.1 deg cells (one multi-coordinate call; the model grid is coarser than the cells, so several cells share one model point) and drives the headline rain numbers; the GFS 0.25 deg ensemble is stored as a second opinion. Per cell and Lagos day the pipeline records the ensemble-median and 90th-percentile 24-h rain, the chance of at least 20/40/60 mm (share of the 51 series), the peak 3-hour window, the hours at risk (member-median rate at least 10 mm/h, or at least 30% of members at it), whether those hours come within 2 h of an EOT20 high tide, a plain risk level (chance of heavy rain, nudged by this cell's own reported-flood record), and, at medium or above, past days whose rain matched the forecast (analogues). Each cell also carries the 168-hour member-median and 90th-percentile rain rate in mm/h for the UI. GloFAS river ensembles and their 1984-present daily-flow history are fetched for two river points, and each forecast day is flagged when the member-median flow reaches the point's historical 90th/99th percentile. Raw API responses are cached under pipeline/cache/forecast/2026-10-21/ (ecmwf_ifs025.json, flood_ogun-ishi_ensemble.json, flood_ogun-ishi_history.json, flood_owo-ikorodu_ensemble.json, flood_owo-ikorodu_history.json, gfs025.json) and reused on same-day reruns, so an archived run stays reproducible.

models.rivers: GloFAS via the Open-Meteo Flood API (control + 50 perturbed members)
models.tide: EOT20 (17 constituents, computed locally with pyTMD)

rules.risk_window: An hour is inside the risk window when the member-median rain rate is at least 10 mm/h, or at least 30% of the 51 ensemble series reach 10 mm/h in that hour; consecutive hours are joined into ranges in Lagos time. A day's window is flagged near_high_tide when any of its hours falls within +/- 2 h of a high tide.
rules.hourly_rate_justification: 10 mm/h is the low end of what preceded reported flood days in the satellite record: on each of the 87 reported flood days, the highest 30-min IMERG rain rate over all 68 cells on the day itself or the day before has a 10th percentile of 8.9 mm/h and a median of 21.9 mm/h, and 74 of 87 days reached 10 mm/h somewhere in the city. Hourly ensemble precipitation (mm per hour) is compared against that rate directly.
rules.risk_level: The level starts from the chance of heavy rain (high: at least 30% chance of 40 mm in 24 h; medium: at least 10%; low: at least 20% chance of 20 mm; none below that), then moves one step by this cell's own record when it has at least 5 past days of the forecast's size class (10-20 / 20-40 / 40+ mm, April-November of the searched months, 2014 onward): one step up if at least a quarter of those days were reported floods within 5 km of the cell centre, one step down if none of them were. In one sentence: heavy rain likely or possible, checked against how often rain of that size here actually flooded.
rules.analogues: For medium and high cell-days: past days (April-November of the searched months, 2014 onward) whose IMERG 24-h total at the cell is within +/- 25% of the forecast median and at least 20 mm. Days with a flood reported within 5 km of the cell centre come first (flood_day), then the closest to the forecast; up to 5 are kept, each with the reported flood areas within 5 km of the cell centre. Counts: n_qualifying_flood_days = qualifying days with a flood reported within 5 km; n_qualifying_citywide_flood_days = qualifying days with a flood reported anywhere in Lagos.
rules.rivers: Per river point: the daily ensemble median and 90th-percentile flow over the forecast days, flagged at_or_above_p90_hist / at_or_above_p99_hist when the median reaches the historical 90th/99th percentile of daily flow at that point (1984-01-01 onward, GloFAS reanalysis).
rules.tides: The EOT20 astronomical tide is computed hourly at the offshore point over the 7 forecast days; every local maximum is listed as a high tide (times to the nearest hour, heights in metres above sea level). No storm surge, no lagoon damping or phase lag is included.

caveats: A reported flood undercounts real floods: the catalog is news coverage, not a gauge, so floods no outlet reported are missing and every 'how often it flooded' number here is a floor, not the truth.
The forecast model is coarser than our history cells: the ECMWF ensemble is 0.25 deg (about 25 km), so several 0.1 deg cells share one model point and neighbourhood rain is smoothed.
The chances are the spread of the model's own ensemble, not true probabilities.
The tide is astronomical only: no storm surge, and the lagoon drains slower than the open sea, so the real high water inside Lagos can be different.
River flow is modelled (GloFAS), not measured; there is no public gauge for the Ogun at Kara or the Osun/Owo outlet.
Forecasts get less reliable further out; by day 7 this is a hint, not a plan.
Satellite rain (IMERG) smooths storm cores, so the heaviest burst in a cell can be heavier than the cell number shows.
